::: {.hero}
## From quantitative proteomes to biological insight

**ProtVis** combines data import, Raw/mzML database search, preprocessing, quality control, statistical analysis, functional interpretation, multi-omics integration, PTM analysis, and publication-ready visualization in one interactive workflow. This cookbook follows the application in the same order that a real project is analyzed.

[Start with installation](content/installation.qmd) · [Run Raw/mzML + Sage](content/data_import/raw_sage_search.qmd) · [Understand `ProtVis_dataset`](content/reproducibility/ProtVis_dataset.qmd)
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Documentation version
This edition is aligned to **ProtVis 0.7.9 on the `dev` branch**, reviewed on **2026-09-13**. ProtVis is under active development; the cookbook emphasizes stable concepts and explicitly identifies compatibility behavior where relevant.
:::

## ProtVis at a glance

The overview below shows how heterogeneous proteomics software outputs are brought into `ProtVis_dataset`, processed through a shared preprocessing and quality-control workflow, and connected to differential analysis, functional interpretation, multi-omics, WGCNA, and key-protein characterization.

![Overview Workflow in ProtVis. Heterogeneous proteomics software outputs enter a unified `ProtVis_dataset` workflow spanning preprocessing, data summary, downstream analysis, multi-omics integration, WGCNA, and key-protein characterization.](images/protvis-overview-workflow.svg){#fig-protvis-overview-workflow fig-alt="Overview of the ProtVis workflow. MaxQuant, Proteome Discoverer, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe, Skyline, OpenMS, and user-defined matrices feed into ProtVis_dataset. The workflow includes noise correction, data transformation, missing-value imputation, normalization, data summary, differential abundance analysis, enrichment, GSEA, pathway analysis, multi-omics analysis, WGCNA, and key-protein functional and modification analyses." width="95%" fig-align="center"}

<div class="feature-grid">
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Heterogeneous input</strong>
<p>Import MaxQuant, Proteome Discoverer, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe, Skyline, OpenMS, Mascot, or a user-defined matrix.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Raw/mzML + Sage</strong>
<p>Register sample metadata, validate mzML filenames, upload a protein FASTA, run Sage, and convert LFQ results directly into the canonical project object.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Traceable data object</strong>
<p>Carry expression data, sample and protein metadata, annotations, results, imported files, parameters, and process history in <code>ProtVis_dataset</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Proteomics preprocessing</strong>
<p>Correct replicate-level noise, transform intensities, inspect missingness, impute missing values, and normalize samples.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>QC and statistics</strong>
<p>Use correlation, expression-pattern heatmaps, PCA/PCoA/t-SNE/UMAP/NMDS, proteomics QC, and limma-based differential abundance analysis.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Biological interpretation</strong>
<p>Continue from DEP results into GO/KEGG enrichment, GSEA, Pathview, STRINGdb PPI, WGCNA, and co-enrichment.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Beyond standard proteomics</strong>
<p>Explore metaproteomics, expression profiles, nine-quadrant integration, Venn analysis, PTMs, strict spectra, and protein structure utilities.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Recommended analysis paths

For **Raw/mzML data**, use:

**Project init → Search → Correct Noise → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization → Overview → DEP → Interpretation**

For **MaxQuant**, use:

**Project init → MaxQuant Output Preparation → Correct Noise → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization → Overview → DEP → Interpretation**

For **other supported tabular outputs**, import/parse the source-specific quantitative table and continue into the shared preprocessing workflow.

The Raw route is intentionally different: Project init can create a sample-only Sage staging `ProtVis_dataset` without inventing an expression matrix. The protein-by-sample matrix is created after the Sage LFQ search succeeds.

## Two ways to learn ProtVis

**GUI-first users** can follow the chapter order in the sidebar. Each page explains prerequisites, the controls to use, expected outputs, and common failure points.

**Reproducible-workflow users** should also read [`ProtVis_dataset`](content/reproducibility/ProtVis_dataset.qmd) and [Checkpoints & recovery](content/reproducibility/checkpoints.qmd). These chapters explain how ProtVis preserves analysis provenance and how projects can be resumed without rebuilding every previous step.
